copy.blurb:
FIFA World Cup 2026 on Thursday, afternoon UTC kickoff, brings Czechia and South Africa together. The Desk's read disagrees with the market on the Czechia side, by +14.6pp — and that disagreement is the Pick.

The Elo prior reads Czechia 1830 vs South Africa 1620: 210 points in favour of Czechia, which is a meaningful but not decisive prior. Both Elo numbers are pulled live from the public Elo source. No host, home-ground, or altitude adjustments apply here; the prior reads straight from Elo.

Three-way split from the model: Czechia to win at 64%, the draw at 17%, and South Africa to win at 19%. The Desk's three-way distribution is calibrated against the W/D/L resolution Polymarket and Kalshi settle on, not against the exact scoreline. Czechia sits at 64% of the mass.

On the same three-way, Polymarket: Czechia to win at 49%, the draw at 28%, and South Africa to win at 22%. The Czechia side trades at 49% on Polymarket, which prices out at American odds of +104. That's where the engine differs: our number reads 64%, +14.6pp wider.

The +3pp Pick threshold isn't on the point estimate, it's on the 5th-percentile from a 100-sample bootstrap of the Elo prior plus bonuses. On Czechia, that haircut lands the model at 55%; the market is at 49%. Even on the conservative reading, the gap is +6.1pp. We're not arguing the market is broadly wrong; the closing line and the model are in approximate agreement across recent fixtures by Brier score. The claim is narrower: this side specifically reads mispriced.

This number will move. Confirmed starting elevens, injuries, weather at the venue, and suspensions carried in from previous fixtures all re-enter the prior on the late-binding cadence. With kickoff 30 days out, we're still on weekly refresh; the daily cadence picks up inside T-5d. The Pick can flip to a Pass if news moves enough of the prior. The Desk does not tip and does not recommend a trade — the model price, the market price, and the gap across them are what's on the page.
drivers: Pre-tournament Elo gives Czechia a stronger prior than the Polymarket line implies.
The +14.6pp gap clears our 3 percentage point threshold for a Pick.
Calibration sits with the closing market across recent fixtures, so selection is the lever.
Late-binding signals — form, confirmed XI, weather — re-evaluate closer to kickoff.
copy.summary: On every meaningful read, Czechia look stronger here than Polymarket has them. Model 64% vs market 49% — a +14.6pp gap on the favourite side.
copy.title: Czechia v South Africa · the model leans Czechia
